entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Chanakya?
entries.text: Chanakya (IAST: Cāṇakya; c. 350-283 BCE) was an adviser and Prime minister to Chandragupta Maurya (c. 340-293 BCE). He played a key role in helping Chandragupta in the establishment of Maurya Empire.
entries.title: Chanakya

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Socrates?
entries.text: Socrates (399 BC-470 BC) was one of the most famous Greek philosophers. He showed how argument, debate, and discussion could help people to understand difficult issues.
entries.title: Socrates

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Suleiman the Magnificent?
entries.text: Suleiman I, commonly known as Suleiman the Magnificent in Western Europe and Suleiman the Lawgiver (Ottoman Turkish: قانونى سلطان سليمان, romanized: Ḳānūnī Sulṭān Süleymān) in his Ottoman realm, was the tenth Sultan of the Ottoman Empire. He became sultan when he was 26 years old.
entries.title: Suleiman the Magnificent

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Sun Yat-sen?
entries.text: Sun Wen, Sun Zhongshan or Sun Yat-sen (12 November 1866 – 12 March 1925) was born in China and was a Chinese political leader. On his 8th attempt while living in Maui Sun helped overthrow the Qing Dynasty in October 1911 during the Xinhai Revolution.
entries.title: Sun Yat-sen

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Ernest Rutherford?
entries.text: Ernest Rutherford, 1st Baron Rutherford of Nelson OM PC FRS (30 August 1871 – 19 October 1937) was a New Zealand-born British scientist. He won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1908 for his work on nuclear physics, and for his theory of the structure of the atom.
entries.title: Ernest Rutherford

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Antonín Dvořák?
entries.text: Antonín Leopold Dvořák (8 September 1841 – 1 May 1904) was a Czech composer. Along with Smetana and Janáček, Dvorak is one of three famous composers who wrote nationalist Czech music.
entries.title: Antonín Dvořák

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Geoffrey Chaucer?
entries.text: Geoffrey Chaucer (c. 1343–25 October 1400) was an English writer, poet, and philosopher. He is most famous for writing Canterbury Tales, his estate satire about a group of pilgrims traveling from London to Canterbury and telling tales to pass the time.
entries.title: Geoffrey Chaucer

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: Who was Charles Dickens?
entries.text: Charles Dickens (7 February 1812 – 9 June 1870) was an English writer and a social critic who is regarded as one of the great English writers of the 19th century.
entries.title: Charles Dickens

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Dialectic?
entries.text: In philosophy, dialectic is a debate or an argument between different individuals. In medieval Europe, dialectics (or logic) was one of the three beginning liberal arts known as the trivium altogether, while the others were grammar and rhetoric.
entries.title: Dialectic

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is God?
entries.text: God is a being or spirit worshipped as a deity. God is considered to be the creator of the universe in some religions.
entries.title: God

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Soul?
entries.text: Many philosophies and religions say that a soul is a supernatural essence of a living human being that lives after death. It is usually said to be immortal.
entries.title: Soul

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Taoism?
entries.text: Taoism or Daoism (道教) is both a philosophy and religion originated in China, which has 2,500 years of history.
entries.title: Taoism

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Education?
entries.text: Education is about learning skills and knowledge. It also means helping people to learn how to do things and support them to think about what they learn.
entries.title: Education

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Euro?
entries.text: Euro or € is the currency of the countries in the eurozone. One euro is divided into 100 cent (officially) (singular) or "cents" (unofficially).
entries.title: Euro

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is United Nations?
entries.text: The United Nations (UN) is an organization between countries established on 24 October 1945 to promote international cooperation. It was founded to replace the League of Nations following World War II and to prevent another conflict.
entries.title: United Nations

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Language?
entries.text: Language is the normal way humans communicate. Only humans use language, though other animals communicate through other means.
entries.title: Language

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Latin?
entries.text: Latin is an Italic language that was developed in Ancient Rome. Short Latin texts have been found from about the 5th century BC and longer texts from about the 3rd century BC.
entries.title: Latin

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Milky Way?
entries.text: The Milky Way is our home galaxy. It contains around 400 billion stars, including our Sun.
entries.title: Milky Way

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Life?
entries.text: Life is matter that can make more of itself. It is separated by non-living matter.
entries.title: Life

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Plant?
entries.text: Plants are one of six big groups (kingdoms) of living things. They are autotrophic eukaryotes, this means they have complex cells, and make their own food.
entries.title: Plant

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Human digestive system?
entries.text: The digestive system is a part of the body that digests food. It is called the gastrointestinal system.
entries.title: Human digestive system

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Liver?
entries.text: The liver is an organ in the abdomen. It is part of the digestive system.
entries.title: Liver

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Brain?
entries.text: The brain is the part of the body which lets living beings think. It does some bodily functions, such as telling the rest of the body what to do.
entries.title: Brain

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Medicine?
entries.text: Medicine is the science that treats and prevents diseases in humans. Medical workers treat injuries, infections, and sickness.
entries.title: Medicine

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Dentistry?
entries.text: Dentistry is a specialty in medicine, which is practiced by a dentist. Dentists find out what's wrong, fix, and help prevent problems with teeth.
entries.title: Dentistry

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Disability?
entries.text: A disability is a condition that a person has which limits them in some way. These conditions may be congenital (present at birth), cognitive (associated with the brain), developmental (appears as the person develops) and physical, which can be caused by an accident or infection.
entries.title: Disability

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Chemical compound?
entries.text: A chemical compound is a substance made of two or more different elements joined together by chemical bonds in a fixed ratio. Many compounds are made of separate molecules.
entries.title: Chemical compound

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Vacuum?
entries.text: A vacuum is a place where there is no matter, not even air. Sound cannot move in a vacuum.
entries.title: Vacuum

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Irrigation?
entries.text: Irrigation is when people add water to plants, to help them grow when there is not enough rain. Irrigation water can be pumped from rivers, natural lakes or lakes created by dams, from wells or allowed to flow to the fields by or open canals.
entries.title: Irrigation

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Central processing unit?
entries.text: A central processing unit (CPU) is an important part of every computer. The CPU sends signals to control the other parts of the computer, almost like how a brain controls a body.
entries.title: Central processing unit

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Operating system?
entries.text: An operating system (OS) is a kind of computer program that helps a computer to interact with other machines or with people. An OS is not actually one single program but a group of small programs, like file managers, device drivers, and kernels.
entries.title: Operating system

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Culture?
entries.text: Culture is a word for the 'way of life' of groups of people, meaning the way they do things. Different groups may have different cultures.
entries.title: Culture

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Nazi Germany?
entries.text: Nazi Germany (officially known as the German Reich from 1933 to 1943, later known as the Greater German Reich from 1943 to 1945; commonly simply called Germany), was the period of Germany between 1933 and 1945.
entries.title: Nazi Germany

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Vietnam?
entries.text: The Socialist Republic of Vietnam (or just Vietnam) (Vietnamese: Cộng hòa Xã hội chủ nghĩa Việt Nam) is a country in Southeast Asia. The neighboring countries are Cambodia, China, and Laos.
entries.title: Vietnam

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Argentina?
entries.text: Argentina, officially the Argentine Republic, is a country in South America. Argentina is the second-largest country in South America and the eighth-largest country in the world.
entries.title: Argentina

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is New York City?
entries.text: New York, often called New York City (NYC), is the most populous city in the U.S. state of New York, and the largest city in the United States. It is at the southern end of the U.S. state of New York.

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.question: What is Capital city?
entries.text: A capital city, or capital town or capital, is a city or town, specified by law or constitution, by the government of a country, or part of a country, such as a state, province, or county. It usually serves as the location of the government's central meeting place and offices.
entries.title: Capital city

entries.text: An atlas is a collection of maps or manifolds, traditionally bound into book form, but also found in multimedia formats.

entries.text: The East Siberian Sea is a marginal sea in the Arctic Ocean. It is between the Arctic Cape to the north, the coast of Siberia to the south, the New Siberian Islands to the west and Cape Billings, close to Chukotka, and Wrangel Island to the east.

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.text: The Strait of Dover or Dover Strait is the strait at the narrowest part of the English Channel.

entries.text: The Rio Negro is a river which flows through the Amazon rainforest in north-western Brazil, in the state of Amazonas.

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.question: What is Lake Eyre?
entries.text: Lake Eyre (pronounced "air") is the lowest point in Australia, at about 15 m (49 ft) below sea level. When it fills with water, it is the largest lake in Australia, being 144 km (89 mi) long and 77 km (48 mi) wide.
entries.title: Lake Eyre

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Canary Islands?
entries.text: The Canary Islands are an autonomous community of Spain located off the coast of Africa. entries.title: Canary Islands

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.text: Hispaniola is an island in the Caribbean Sea. It is the second largest island (after Cuba) of the West Indies, east of Cuba and west of Puerto Rico.

entries.text: Greenland is the world's largest island. Greenland is a self-governing territory of the kingdom of Denmark.

entries.text: Luzon is an major island in the Philippines. It is situated at northern portion of the country.

entries.text: Corsica is an island in the Mediterranean Sea. It is west of Tuscany, southeast of France, south of Liguria and north of the island of Sardinia.
entries.title: Corsica

entries.text: K2 is the second-highest mountain in the world, standing at 8,611 metres (28,251 ft) tall. It is also known as Mount Godwin-Austen or Chogori (ཆོགོ་རི།).

entries.text: Lorentz National Park is a national park in Papua, Indonesia. It has an area of about 25,056 kilometres (15,569 mi).

entries.text: Colombo (Sinhala: කොළඹ; Tamil: கொழும்பு) is the largest city of Sri Lanka. It is the city which is economically most important to the country.

entries.text: Kabul is the capital and largest city of Afghanistan.

entries.text: Addis Ababa (also spelled Addis Abeba) is the capital city of Ethiopia. It is also the political capital of the African Union.

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.text: Santiago (also known as Santiago de Chile) is the capital of Chile and the largest city in the country. It has a population of around 7 million people, about 40 percent of the population of Chile.

entries.text: Vilnius is the largest city and the capital of Lithuania, with a population of 553,904 (850,700 together with Vilnius County) as of December 2005. It is the seat of the Vilnius city municipality and of the Vilnius district municipality.
entries.title: Vilnius

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.text: Liverpool is a city in North West England, United Kingdom with a population of about 485,000 in 2015. It is part of the Liverpool-Birkenhead metropolitan area, the fifth-largest metropolitan area in the UK.

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.text: Perth (Nyungar: Boorloo) is the capital city of the state of Western Australia. It is built on the banks of the Swan River.

entries.title: Cook Islands

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.title: Faroe Islands

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.text: Haiti (Haitian Creole: Ayiti; French: Haïti), officially the Republic of Haiti (Haitian Creole: Repiblik d Ayiti; French: République d'Haïti) is a country on the Caribbean island of Hispaniola. The other country on the island is the Dominican Republic.

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.title: Astrometry

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.title: Celestial equator

entries.text: In astronomy, the nadir is a point "below" a particular location. "Below" means in the same direction of gravity at that location.

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.text: Virgo is a zodiac constellation which lies on the celestial equator. It is between Leo (at west) and Libra (at east).This constellation is large; the constellation is the second biggest constellation you can see on the sky.

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Spiral galaxy?
entries.text: A spiral galaxy is a kind of galaxy that looks like a flat, slowly rotating disk with a bulge in the centre, and spiral patterns extending outward from the bulge. It contains stars, gas, dust, dark matter and a supermassive black hole at its centre.
entries.title: Spiral galaxy

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.question: What is Starburst galaxy?
entries.text: A starburst galaxy is a galaxy with a very high rate of star formation. The rate of star formation is so large that the galaxy will quickly use all of its gas reservoir (from which the stars are made).
entries.title: Starburst galaxy

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.title: Density

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors

entries.text: Metrology is the study of Measurements. It starts a common understanding of units for human uses.

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.text: SC Eisenstadt was an Austrian association football club from Eisenstadt. It was founded in 1907 and played in the Austrian Football Bundesliga 13 seasons. They last played in the Bundesliga in the 1986-87 season. It was dissolved in 2008 for financial reasons. In 2018 SC Eisenstadt was newly founded and started in the lowest league (2. Klasse Nord) in Burgenland. They also train around 100 children in their youth teams.
entries.title: SC Eisenstadt

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.text: Taoism or Daoism (道教) is both a philosophy and religion originated in China, which has 2,500 years of history. Tao (or Dao, 道) is the name of the force or the Way that Taoists believe makes everything in the world. Taoists think that words cannot be used to correctly describe Tao. The very first line of the Dào Dé Jīng (道德經), the most important text in Taoism, says that: the Way that can be explained in words is not the true Way. There are many other sacred writings by the teachers of Taoism. Instead of spending a lot of time trying to explain what the Tao is, Taoists focus on living a simple and balanced life in harmony with nature. This is one of the most important principles in Taoism. Taoists also believe that conflict is not good and that if you have an issue, it is better to get around with it.
entries.title: Taoism

entries.author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
entries.text: An alphabet is a writing system, a list of symbols for writing. The basic symbols in an alphabet are called letters. In an alphabet, each letter is a symbol for a sound or related sounds. To make the alphabet work better, more signs assist the reader: punctuation marks, spaces, standard reading direction, and so on. The symbols are in a strict ordered list, called alphabetical order. The name alphabet comes from Aleph and Beth, the first two letters in the Phoenician alphabet. This article is written with the Roman alphabet (or Latin alphabet). It was first used in Ancient Rome to write Latin. Many languages use the Latin alphabet: it is the most used alphabet today.
entries.title: Alphabet
